atoms.micro_check: Identify the direction of an upward velocity arrow.

atoms.proposition: A chosen positive direction determines signs.
atoms.micro_check: With upward positive, assign the sign of a downward vector.

atoms.proposition: Velocity includes direction as well as magnitude.
Acceleration describes how velocity changes with time.
atoms.micro_check: Describe the change 22 -> 12 m/s in one second.

atoms.proposition: Negative acceleration does not imply negative velocity.
atoms.micro_check: Can velocity be upward while acceleration is downward? Explain.

atoms.proposition: Constant acceleration gives equal velocity changes in equal time intervals.
Motion events use a defined clock origin and elapsed interval.
atoms.micro_check: Mark launch at t=0 and the stated event at t=1 s.

atoms.proposition: A velocity may be resolved into horizontal and vertical components.
atoms.micro_check: Identify v_x and v_y on a velocity arrow.

atoms.proposition: In the ideal near-Earth model gravity accelerates vertically downward.
atoms.micro_check: Draw the acceleration arrow at the top of the flight.

atoms.proposition: Horizontal velocity does not create vertical acceleration in ideal projectile motion.
atoms.micro_check: Predict which of two equal-height balls lands first: dropped or pushed sideways.

atoms.proposition: A time-velocity table represents successive vertical velocity states.
atoms.micro_check: Read v_y at t=2 s from a table.

atoms.proposition: A velocity-time graph represents the same states as a time-velocity table.
atoms.micro_check: Plot table values and identify where v_y=0.

atoms.proposition: The slope of a velocity-time graph is acceleration.
atoms.micro_check: Explain what a -10 m/s per second slope means physically.

atoms.proposition: u_y, v_y, a_y and t label already-understood vertical-motion quantities.
atoms.micro_check: Match each symbol to its physical quantity.

atoms.proposition: v_y = u_y + a_y t compresses starting velocity plus accumulated constant velocity change.
atoms.micro_check: Explain the equation in words before substituting numbers.
